correctness.rationale: The incidence-mask two-list constraint is necessary and sufficient for every received output. All fixed-weight binary codebooks at n=2,3,4,5 were exhaustively enumerated at the asserted optimal sizes and the next size; maxima counts were nonzero and next-level counts zero. A separate three-word shortest common supersequence/longest common subsequence DP independently reconstructed forbidden triples and repeated every optimum/count. Downward closure excludes larger sizes, and an exhaustive orbit partition checks all 185 five-bit insertion maxima. No infinite-length extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: This determines the first finite alphabet-length separation between the maximum numbers of codewords supporting two-list decoding after an equal two-insertion versus two-deletion budget, for each admissible binary length up to the sharp cutoff. It additionally classifies all 185 insertion-optimal codebooks into 52 natural symmetry classes. The exact threshold, extremizers, and two-error asymmetry address a natural finite analogue of a developing list-decoding literature; none is a routine rescaling of existing n=6 deletion-only tables.
